reasoning: The registry search closes the gap behind the earlier false verdict. It is a structured search of all 11 JSONL files: 37,669 records, a total that matches the per-file counts, each file with its SHA-256 recorded, aliases and unused entries included. It looked for the /6 root and descendants, the Hebrew consonants with and without the vav, and the variant transliterations. Its only hit was the existing fifth_day/6. No exact identity and no child exists to reuse.

The corpus search of 18,093 XML files finds this couplet only inside Thursday /6. So the text already has an identity root, and reuse under that root is required. Minting a new prayer: root would give one text two URNs, which breaks the registry's purpose: 'one text has exactly one URN' (SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME.md:578-579).

The Sunday closing has the same words as the last couplet of /6. The only differences are orthography, the form of the divine Name (ה׳ versus יְיָ), the lack of pointing and punctuation. None of these creates a new identity. All of /6 is too broad, because it would bring in three couplets that Sunday does not print.

SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME.md:536-542 prefers a named subdivision to a numeric one. A number is the edition's own count, so it can change between editions and claims an alignment that does not exist. The couplet has a natural name, its incipit, so the named child is the correct form and the earlier /6/4 recommendation is replaced.

One canonical realization per project is consistent with the scheme's rule that each distinct text is mapped canonically once, with repeats carrying @source. s327 holds both occurrences. Making Sunday the canonical home and annotating the Thursday occurrence avoids a duplicate corresp mapping while keeping the Thursday words and the /6 scope intact.

The new witness does not require editing 1150. The registry records known branches and never asserts that every project realizing the parent implements them. The child stays bound by identity to the last couplet of Thursday /6 through its path and its parent record, even though only the new edition realizes it.
No partition of /6 is needed. Registering one used child is enough, and inventing sibling names would register branches that nothing uses.
